concerns.text: The 'Perfect Low-Level Executor' is defined as 'a high-fidelity simulation with ground-truth physics'. This is causally circular for the hypothesis under test: the Oracle embodies exactly the continuous physics fidelity the project claims is unnecessary, so the 'Physics Fidelity Gap' (SC-006) conflates planner logic with physics-engine fidelity and violates Constitution Principle VI (metrics must be decoupled from physics fidelity). Replace with a deterministic, non-physics rule-based verifier of symbolic-sequence validity against the ground-truth task graph.

Wilcoxon signed-rank on 18 paired binary outcomes is statistically ill-suited: with binary per-task outcomes the test degenerates toward a sign test, discards effect-size information, and has very low power at N=18 (no power analysis or multiple-trials-per-task design is specified). Either run multiple execution trials per task to obtain graded success rates, or use an exact paired test for binary data (e.g., McNemar/exact binomial on discordant pairs) with an explicit power statement.

The Symbolic-vs-Neural comparison confounds the symbolic abstraction variable with the low-level controller adaptation (FR-009): the symbolic system uses an adapted controller while the baseline uses the original policy, and no 'Neural+Oracle' control exists, so failure attribution between planning and execution cannot be isolated for the baseline. The spec should either restrict the claim to system-level comparison or add the missing control condition.

The embedding→SymbolicState mapping is treated as deterministic, but it is a noisy perception step. No requirement validates mapping accuracy (e.g., predicate-level precision/recall against annotated ground truth), so 'Planner Infeasibility' failures (FR-006) are confounded with encoder/mapping errors. Add an FR measuring mapping accuracy independently of planner outcomes.
